variant_desc: 100k chunks each w/ private 2048-int buffer + per-chunk memcpy compaction -> shared buffer + per-chunk selection-vector (no memcpy) (variant 2: seed=44, n_scale=1.5x)
source_citation: Qiao & Zhang, 'Compacting Vectorized Execution' (SIGMOD'25); DuckDB PR #14956 (up to 3x on head-to-head microbenchmark).
novelty_rationale: Tests recognition that when ~40% of chunks contain a single valid element (the DuckDB CRF=2048 measurement), the per-chunk physical compaction (memcpy + scan setup) costs more than the actual data work. Logical compaction with a shared buffer + per-chunk selection vector amortizes the setup. Compilers cannot perform this transformation because it requires redesigning the per-chunk data structure based on observed runtime cardinality distributions.
